data.description:
## Problem

`src/rebar/similar/index.py` recovers from a corrupt or version-stale index by calling
`_discard(path)` — which unlinks the database file and its `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars — and then
rebuilding via `_open_one`. That path carries **no lock**.

Every other write in the subsystem serializes on sqlite's own write lock: `catchup.py` opens
its transaction with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` under a `busy_timeout`, and `catchup.py`'s module
docstring states "Concurrent reconcilers serialize on sqlite's write lock." The
discard-and-rebuild path is an unlocked twin of that write path — `os.unlink` is not covered
by a sqlite lock, and there is no flock or `threading.Lock` anywhere under `src/rebar/similar`.

## Why two executors can reach it at once

`open_index` is called independently by each MCP request handler on the create path
(`src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py` serves concurrent handlers on a worker thread). `_open_one`
raises `StaleIndex`/`sqlite3.DatabaseError` for **both** callers before either has finished
rebuilding, so both enter the recovery branch.

## Harm

Two interleavings, both silent:

1. Executor B's `os.unlink(path + "-wal")` removes the WAL sidecar of executor A's live
   connection, leaving A's FTS5 state inconsistent.
2. Executor A commits its catch-up rows into an inode that B's later unlink has detached. The
   on-disk index then silently loses those rows and serves empty results until the next full
   rebuild.

Both produce exactly the failure mode ADR 0122's design set out to avoid: a silently frozen
index is indistinguishable from a healthy index that matched nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The discard-and-rebuild path in `src/rebar/similar/index.py` is serialized against
      itself, so two concurrent callers that both observe a corrupt or stale index produce
      one rebuild rather than two interleaved ones.
- [ ] A test starts two threads that both hit the recovery branch on the same index path
      (barrier-synchronized, as `test_concurrent_catch_up_runs_leave_a_sound_index_holding_both_tickets`
      already does for the normal write path) and asserts afterwards that
      `PRAGMA integrity_check` returns `ok` and that every ticket written before the
      corruption is still retrievable.
- [ ] That test fails against the current unsynchronized implementation.
- [ ] If the chosen fix adds a lock, it carries a `# mechanism-ok: lock <name> — <reason>`
      marker at its definition site, since the mechanism-delta ratchet fails on any
      unadmitted new mechanism.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Provenance

Found by `rebar review-code` as an advisory finding on ticket `47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88`'s change
(Change-Id `I3e1c9d8fa0c95a152b9be91ed8357a6ad2389e73`). Three sibling advisories from the same
review — a `limit <= 0` off-by-one, an `UNKNOWN_MTIME` sentinel compared by equality, and an
inaccurate warm-path docstring — were fixed inside 47c8 itself. This one is deferred because
it is a design change to the recovery path rather than a localized correction, and because the
race predates the reviewed change in shape: it is a property of the recovery branch, not of
the new indexing code.
data.title: Serialize the similar-index discard-and-rebuild path
